summary: In Greek mythology, Eurytus or Erytus (Ancient Greek: Εὔρυτος / Ἔρυτος) of Alope was a son of Hermes and Antianeira (or Laothoe), brother of Echion, and an Argonaut. Apollonius describes the brothers as "well skilled in craftiness"; Hyginus also counts him among the hunters of the Calydonian boar. He is distinct from Eurytus king of Oechalia and from the Giant of the same name.

sections.heading: Son of Hermes
paragraphs: Eurytus (also Erytus) of Alope was son of Hermes by Antianeira daughter of Menetus, or by Laothoe in a variant; his brother was Echion, and Aethalides is sometimes named as a stepbrother. As children of the thief-god, Apollonius describes Erytus and Echion as "well skilled in craftiness," signifying the craft they inherit from Hermes.

sections.heading: Argonaut and boar hunter
paragraphs: Apollonius Rhodius (Argonautica 1.51–54) and Apollodorus (Bibliotheca 1.9.16) list Eurytus among the Argonauts who sailed from Alope with his brother Echion. Hyginus (Fabulae 14, 160, 173) pairs them among the Minyae who sailed with Jason and also places Eurytus at the Calydonian boar hunt.
Beyond these catalogue appearances he has little separate myth; his fame is genealogical and crew-list rather than episodic.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: This atlas entry (eurytus-hermes) is the Argonaut son of Hermes. Distinct from Eurytus king of Oechalia (eurytus-oechalia); from the Giant slain by Dionysus (eurytus-giant); from the Epeian leader at Troy (eurytus-epeian); and from other minor Eurytuses on the Wikipedia disambiguation page.
